[LGRA.22.3] **The grammar with the single `NAME` terminal is unambiguous.**
Every input has at most one parse. A `NAME` reachable under two productions at
one state is permitted only where the productions build the same AST node
(expression atoms, call heads) or where a following token of a distinct class
separates them.

**This is a property of the language, not of a parsing technique.** An
implementation may recognise the language with any parser that accepts exactly
this grammar: conformance turns on what it accepts, not on how. A zero-conflict
LR table built from a fixed BNF desugaring of these productions is evidence of
the property, sufficient and not necessary.
gap_reason: No tool checks the grammar's unambiguity. The Mercury compiler's parser is hand-written and builds no table, and a check over the text of [LGRA]'s productions does not exist.
